Give the code a clear place in the review.

CodeRabbit Change Stack · Formbricks #8650 · Parth Pawar · October 19, 2026

A reviewer needs to locate a change, understand its explanation, and decide what to do next. The redesign keeps layer-based review, with stable navigation, a focused code workspace, and explicit context scope.

Observed in the assigned reviewDesign decision and expected benefit
Layer, file, semantic, and context toolbars compete with the code.One sticky file toolbar groups frequent actions. The compact PR header holds the final review action. Secondary tools keep labeled destinations.
Seven layers and a nine-file first layer require repeated orientation.Keep the selected layer and filename together. A file-position control opens all nine verified paths without filling the rail with a long tree.
The context panel has 37 layer summaries; access.ts has six.State file versus layer scope. Selecting a captured summary reveals and highlights its exact range. Preserve complexity labels and disclose uncaptured summaries.
Summary seen, file viewed, and final review are separate progress signals.Give each a distinct action and count. Selecting content alone completes neither the file nor the review. Z preserves position while hiding surrounding panels.

Paper to prototype

The prototype demonstrates seven-layer navigation, a nine-file picker, seven complete added-file diffs, summary linking, complexity filters, resolved-comment filtering, local drafts, reversible progress, and a simulated decision. Shortcuts ignore typing; dialogs restore focus. Below 1280 px, context opens as an overlay.

Evidence and limits

The exact Formbricks #8650 run initially loaded, then later layer loads and reloads became rate limited. Names/counts, first-layer inventory, summary ranges, and resolved-message state were captured. Seven added files use complete GitHub source at commit 23cdac2. Fourteen summaries are condensed; one resolved thread is paraphrased. Other patches, summaries, and reply bodies are outside the fixture.

The review snapshot is out of date; a resolved historical finding does not establish a current defect. The original capture and redesign use the same PR/file at different visible positions. No measured speed improvement or complete capability parity is claimed. Four product explorations remain optional. Review decisions and drafts are never sent.
